title: Nuclear planning: a pump maintenance window
description: A fictional reference pressurised-water reactor starts paused at full power. Compare one maintenance crew with an extra crew to finish an A-train work window. Pump B stays protected in the plan. Work durations, qualifications, cost and the 17:00 target are authored assumptions; World supplies current pump readings. The plant has no maintenance or isolation state, and Planning never changes it.
objectives: Compare two checked schedules for the same five jobs.
See the hours saved and the additional crew cost.
Ask the Assistant for a heat-transport calculation from current pump flow and explicit assumptions.

guide.title: Is an extra crew worth it?
guide.description: Two separate A-train work sites share one crew. Compare return times with one crew or an extra crew while Pump B is protected in the plan. The pump readings come from this simulation; work duration, cost and target are declared assumptions.

steps.title: Is an extra crew worth it?
steps.instruction: Choose Compare maintenance schedules to see both checked schedules. Work starts at 09:00 with a 17:00 target. The plan reads the two pumps without changing the plant.

steps.title: Inspect the source and ask for a calculation
steps.instruction: Open Planning to compare the crews, then ask the Assistant how much heat the current Pump B flow could carry at a declared temperature rise. This is arithmetic with stated assumptions, not a cooling-system assessment.
